name: Benjamin Kincses
text: The session files sit on disk as plain JSON and anyone with disk access can read the full transcript. Where do you put that directory in a deployed agent, and do you encrypt it or wipe it, or is local disk the wrong place once real user data flows through it?

name: Mayank Raj
text:
The fourteen-stored/six-visible trace makes this much easier to reason about than a generic 'memory' abstraction. One boundary I'd tighten in the manifest example: project an allowlist of application-owned fields into the prompt rather than serializing the whole state dict.

If tool output or user-controlled text later enters state, that bridge can promote untrusted content into the system prompt. Do you see the manifest as a small set of typed invariants, with the rest retrieved only when needed?

name: Robin kumar
text: This highlights an important challenge in AI agent architecture: maintaining consistent context across sessions and conversations. Persisting session data is not enough if the model cannot reliably retrieve and utilize the relevant conversation history. Effective memory management requires a combination of short-term context handling, persistent storage, intelligent retrieval, and context-window optimization. Reliable memory should ensure both continuity across restarts and consistency throughout an active conversation.
